clue.text: Once-revered figure getting a couple of thousand and over

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so two of them give MM
on can mean over, as in a lid on (over) a pot

explanation.surface: Someone once worshipped is now paid two thousand and more.
explanation.walkthrough: Ammon (Amun) was the chief god of ancient Egypt, hence revered once.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammon was an Egyptian deity worshipped in antiquity, a figure of former reverence.

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for playing quietly
to rate someone is an old word for to scold or rebuke them

explanation.surface: Someone softly tells people off, with a cross-reference to another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer to 20 across, CHATTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean talks idly and at length, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Impractical person calling for a fancy roll

indicators.note: calling means saying out loud, so the clue wants the spoken sound of the phrase

parts.note: an ideal list is a roll (list) that is fancied, a wish list

explanation.surface: A dreamer asks for an elaborate bread roll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy roll' looks like a bakery item; read it as an ideal list, a roll of names one would like, which spoken runs together.
explanation.definitionFit: A visionary who pursues perfection over practicality is typically called unrealistic.

clue.text: This could be stained as an alternative

indicators.note: says the letters of stained could be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: Something might end up stained, offered as another option.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing one thing in place of another means choosing it as a substitute.

parts.note: reads like a strict, unbending boss, but firm is the noun: a head of a company

explanation.definitionFit: A board member who runs a company is its executive head.

clue.text: Circumference of a Middle Eastern spirit measure

parts.note: a peri is a fairy-like spirit of Persian mythology
a meter is a measuring device

explanation.surface: Asks about the distance round some exotic gauge of drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' suggests alcohol and 'measure' a tot, but the spirit is a Persian fairy.
explanation.definitionFit: The boundary line around a shape, its outer edge length, is the circumference.

clue.text: Being disrespectful about revolutionary leader is not wise!

indicators.note: about means going around, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: impudent means cheeky, disrespectful

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Insulting a revolutionary leader is unwise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary leader' suggests a figure like Lenin; it means just the first letter of 'revolutionary'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rash, unwise behaviour is described as imprudent: lacking caution.

indicators.note: formulating means putting together into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Coming up with ideas is useful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Helps' reads as a verb but is the plural noun, assistants.
explanation.definitionFit: Assistants are people who help, often called helpers.

parts.note: G is a musical note
ill means bad, as in ill effects

explanation.surface: Points out a bad piece of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The breathing organ on the side of a fish is part of it.

definitions.meaning: to draw in or shrink back, as a muscle does
an agreement or deal made between parties

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means shrink or draw in; as a noun it is a binding agreement or deal.

clue.text: One with nicer disposition and so peaceloving

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: a disposition is an arrangement, so the letters of nicer are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone of kinder temperament is therefore peaceful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disposition' looks like temperament but signals rearranging NICER into RENIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Irenic describes a conciliatory attitude aiming at peace.

clue.text: It's a backward area of Italy

indicators.note: backward tells us to read the words from right to left

parts.note: the letters of it's a, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Claims a region of Italy is underdeveloped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backward area' sounds like a remote district, but 'backward' reverses ITSA.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a province and town in Piedmont, north-west Italy, famous for wine.

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: to jumble is to mix up, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Everyone carried a mixed heap as they had been told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumble' rearranges TOTED into OTTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something allotted has been given out as a share, i.e. allocated.

clue.text: Lands fruit-and that's where the main danger lies

definitions.text: that's where the main danger lies

parts.note: to light on something is to land on it, so lands gives lights
a hip is the fruit of the rose

explanation.surface: Someone lands produce, then is told where the greatest risk is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is the sea; a moored vessel with a beacon marks a hazard such as a sandbank.
explanation.definitionFit: A moored vessel carrying a beacon is stationed to warn ships of a hazard at sea.

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so one piece goes into another

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
post is Latin for after, as in postwar

explanation.surface: A reply arrives, rightly, once something has been admitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entering' puts POST inside IE.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick retort, a sharp reply.

parts.note: workers on strike are out
the Tories are the political right in Britain

explanation.surface: Conservatives are completely impressive.
explanation.walkthrough: Tories are members of Britain's Conservative Party, on the right wing.
explanation.definitionFit: Outright means completely, without reservation.

clue.text: The individual struggling to hold Her Majesty's dog

indicators.note: to hold means to contain, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: one struggling to do something tries, so is a trier
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A struggling person keeps hold of the Queen's dog.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrier is a breed type of small hunting canine.

indicators.note: varied means changed around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A magistrate wants teatime at different hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judge' is a verb here, to reckon roughly.
explanation.definitionFit: To judge a quantity is to make a rough guess at it.

clue.text: Stupid, which is a shortcoming in a way

parts.note: a sin is a moral failing or shortcoming
taken as written
E, east, is a direction or way to go

explanation.surface: Calls something foolish a failing of sorts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a way' reads as 'in some sense'; here it is IN plus E, east, a direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine means silly or foolish, like a donkey.

clue.text: 2 a mad character in the Civil Service

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: CS is the abbreviation for the Civil Service
the Mad Hatter is a character in Alice in Wonderland

explanation.surface: A lunatic figure working among the government's officials, cross-referenced.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 2 down, PRATES.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean babbles or talks idly, so they are synonyms.

parts.note: er is the sound of audible hesitation
to go is to proceed

explanation.surface: Someone hesitatingly goes ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergo is Latin for therefore, used to draw a conclusion.

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: turn means turn round, so the word to is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone was made to turn towards an explosion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' reverses the second TO, giving OT.
explanation.definitionFit: A toot is a short blast on a horn or whistle.

clue.text: Having a little gown in grey silk made

indicators.note: a little means just part of the words, so the answer lies inside them

explanation.surface: Possessing a small grey silk dress that was made up.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits in gOWN IN Grey.
explanation.definitionFit: Possessing something means holding it as one's own.

clue.text: Set new record, though it's very demanding

indicators.note: new means made fresh, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: EP, extended play, is a type of record

explanation.surface: Breaking a record, though it was a tough task.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges SET into STE.
explanation.definitionFit: A steep demand is excessive, unreasonably hard.

parts.note: as means like
a king is a member of royalty

explanation.surface: Inviting someone in regal fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking someone to come means inviting them.

indicators.note: maybe suggests a possible rearrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: Perhaps suggest someone by naming them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' rearranges A MENTION.
explanation.definitionFit: To nominate a person is to put them forward as a candidate.
The word means both stingy with money and intoxicated by alcohol.

parts.note: in the song Daisy Bell, Daisy is on a bicycle built for two

explanation.walkthrough: Daisy Bell is an old music-hall song about a bicycle built for two.
explanation.definitionFit: A tandem is a bicycle for two riders, as in the song.
